# Terms of Service

**Draft pending legal review. Not yet in force.**

Last updated: 4 October 2026

## In short

- You may use Salony to run your salon. The app is licensed to you, not sold.
- Your salon's records belong to you and stay on your devices. Keeping a
  backup of the books is your responsibility, because nobody else holds a
  copy of the books and nobody else can restore one. An optional public page
  is not a backup of the salon.
- The app is free. Sync over the internet is optional, uses a relay the
  developer operates, and requires signing in with Apple or Google. Turning
  on a public page uses a separate booking service, also operated by the
  developer, and uses the same account. A subscription per store may apply
  to the relay; if one lapses, the app keeps working and only internet sync
  stops.
- The app is provided as it is, without a warranty, and the developer's
  liability is limited to what the law allows.

The sections below are the agreement itself.

## 1. Agreement

Salony is built and published by one person rather than a company. These
terms call them **the developer**, and the agreement is between you and that
person, covering the Salony application, the optional relay service, and the
optional public-page and booking service. By installing or using Salony you
accept them. If you do not accept them, do not use the app.

If you use Salony on behalf of a business, you confirm that you may accept
these terms for that business.

## 2. Licence

The developer grants you a personal, non-exclusive, non-transferable,
revocable licence to install and use Salony on devices you own or control,
for running your own salon business.

You may not: resell, rent or sublicense the app; remove or obscure notices
in it; reverse engineer it except where law expressly permits; or use it to

## 3. Your data and your backups

Your salon's records are yours. The books are written to your devices and are
not transmitted to the developer.

Because there is no cloud copy of the books, **you are responsible for
keeping backups**. If a device is lost, damaged, wiped or stolen, and it
holds the only copy of your records, those records are gone. A public page,
if you turn one on, holds the brochure you published and the request fields
named in section 5; it is not a backup and cannot restore the books. Salony
provides an encrypted export for exactly this reason; use it, and keep the
archive somewhere other than the device it came from. The passphrase
protecting an export cannot be recovered by anyone, including the developer.

You are also responsible for what you collect about your own customers and
staff, for telling them what you collect where the law requires it, and for
handling their requests about that data — including people who send a
booking request from a public page.

## 4. Acceptable use

You agree not to use Salony, the relay service, or the public-page and
booking service to store or transmit unlawful content, to attack, overload,
scrape or probe those services or other users' devices, to circumvent licence
checks, or to gain access to devices you are not authorised to reach.

If you turn on a public page, you also agree that what you publish there is
yours to stand behind: you will not publish unlawful, misleading or
infringing content, and you will not use booking intake to collect data you
are not allowed to collect. A request from the public page is a request for
your salon to review. It is not a confirmed appointment. A message the
booking service may send is described in section 5; it is not you confirming
a time.

## 5. Public page and booking requests

A public page is optional and off until an owner who is signed in turns it
on. The booking service is not the relay and is not the salon's appointment
book. It does not author salon records and is not a copy of your salon. A
request is not an appointment. It becomes an appointment only after someone
with permission confirms it on a store device.

You choose the link name, what the brochure shows, and whether new requests
are accepted. The brochure may include the services the salon marked public.
A visitor may name more than one of those services, up to the cap the salon
set (1 to 12; if they set none, 12). Email on a request is optional. You
review requests in the app. Confirming a request creates an unassigned
appointment on your devices; rejecting it does not. Staff cannot turn the
page on or confirm or reject requests.

The salon may publish a staff display name and an optional photo on the
public page. That is a public name the salon chose, not the internal staff
record and not a login. Anyone with the link can see it. It is removed from
the public page when the salon stops publishing it.

A status page for one request link shows the store name, the services, the
preferred date and time, and whether the request was received, confirmed, or
rejected. It does not show the visitor's name, phone, email, or note.
Received means the salon will review the request. It does not mean a time
is booked. A completed visit still shows as confirmed on that page.

If the visitor left an email, the booking service may send a message about
the request and, after the visit is marked completed, one message with a
review link. The language is the one chosen on the form (English,
Vietnamese, or Chinese). If that email was already deleted, the review
message is not sent. The review page still works for someone who has the
link. A visitor does not get a Salony account.

A signed-in store device may register a push token with the booking service
so it can be told that a request arrived. This is not the relay. The
notification title is Salony. The body does not contain the visitor's name,
phone, email, the service, the time, the note, or review text. The token is
deleted when the store's public binding is deleted. It is not used for
advertising and it is not written into operational logs.

After a completed visit, the visitor can leave one review: a rating from 1
to 5 and optional text of at most 400 characters. The public page shows the
average and the reviews the salon has not hidden, without the visitor's
name. Hiding a review removes it from the public page and the public
average. The booking service keeps the row. A second submit does not change
the stored review. A request that is not completed cannot be reviewed.

7 days after a store device has saved the request and acknowledged it, the
booking service deletes the visitor's name, phone, email, and note. It keeps
the request id, the store, the services (name, duration, and price as they
were at submit), the preferred date and time, the outcome, the prices that
were shown, and the review, so the status page and the review still open. A
request that has not been collected is still kept at least 30 days.

**Fair-use limits.** The booking service limits how much one store or one
account can use, the same for every store: for example how many requests a
store accepts in a day, how many requests can wait to reach the salon, how
many photos a page keeps, how many emails are sent, and how many stores and
groups one account has. Signing in also limits how many stores one account
can license for internet sync. These limits protect visitors and the service.
When one is reached, a new request or action is refused, or a message is
not sent, and the page or the app says what happened. A request that was
accepted is kept. The limits may change; the handbook lists the current
ones.

People who open the page or send a request do not create a Salony account
and are not parties to this agreement as Salony users. They are contacting
your salon. You are responsible for how you handle that contact.

The booking service is provided on a best-effort basis, like the relay. A
cached brochure may still be readable when new requests cannot be sent. An
interruption of the booking service does not stop you running the salon on
your devices; it stops the public page taking new requests.

Turning the public page off, or deleting the app on one device, does not
remove your responsibility for requests you already accepted into the books.

## 6. Optional paid services

Salony is distributed as a free application. There is nothing to buy inside
it.

Sync over the internet uses a relay service operated by the developer. Using
that relay requires an account, created by signing in with Apple or Google.
Local use, pairing, and sync on the same network do not.

Turning on a public page also requires that account, because the booking
service is the developer's infrastructure. Signing in does not by itself
publish a page. Visitors who send a request do not need, and do not get, an
account.

The relay may require a subscription per store. Where it does:

- The price, billing period and renewal terms are those shown at the point of
  purchase.
- A subscription can be cancelled at any time; cancellation takes effect at
  the end of the paid period.
- When a subscription lapses, devices stop connecting to the relay. **The app
  continues to work**: local operation and sync between devices on the same
  network are not affected. A public page you already turned on is a
  separate service from the relay.
- Payments made through the App Store or Google Play are handled by Apple or
  Google under their terms, including their refund policies.

Deleting the account stops licence renewal for internet sync. It does not
delete your salon data, which remains on your devices. To delete the
account, write to ntqui1502@gmail.com. Signing out on a device is not the
same as deleting the account.

## 7. Availability

The relay service and the booking service are provided on a best-effort
basis. Either may be interrupted for maintenance, or discontinued with
reasonable notice. Because the app is built to work offline, an interruption
of the relay does not stop you running your salon; it stops devices reaching
each other over the internet. An interruption of the booking service does
not stop local work; it stops the public page and new online requests.

## 8. App stores

If you obtained Salony from the App Store or Google Play, that store's terms
